messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: priors when using cholesky_decomposition
parts:
Hi all

I am working in a multivariate model. I have been able to speed up the code by applying the cholesky decomposition. I have a doubt about the proper way to use priors on the correlation matrix when I apply the cholesky decomposition.

Before using the cholesky decomposition, I had been using the corr_y ~ lkj_corr(2.0) prior, it caught my attention that using this prior is slower than not stating any explicit prior.

What is the recommended way to include priors when using the cholesky decomposition? Also, to optimize time

My full stan model is attach

Thank you for your help

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] priors when using cholesky_decomposition
parts:
We recommend using a correlation matrix, and having a uniform
distribution on it is well-defined. The lkj_corr(2.0) regularizes
a bit toward the identity correlation matrix. Indeed it's slower
because it requires more work. We have some plans in place to
add a cholesky_factor_corr type --- it's just waiting for transforms
to be added.

There's not an easy way yet to put a prior on the Cholesky factor
directly because of the required Jacobian, but we are going to add
the LKJ version of that, too. Ben can explain how it works.

For speed and size of output, you don't need to make the cov_matrix
transformed parameters --- you can make them local variables in the model
and they won't be printed. We've usually found it easier to look at the
correlation matrices and scales anyway.

Your deviance won't be the total deviance because you're missing
the multi_normal_cholesky terms.

You can just increment_log_prob(log_lik0), which is already the
sum of the log_lik. Not repeating sub-calculations is always
faster.

Also, this should all get faster if we ever get around to vectorizing
the multi_normal, which we really should be doing for this kind of model.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] priors when using cholesky_decomposition
parts:
The default is a uniform distribution over all correlation
matrices (positive definite, values bounded between -1 and 1).
Because correlation matrices have bounded values, the uniform distribution
is proper.

There's no way to directly place bounds other than (-1,1) on the
correlations. But they're not all free to vary between -1 and 1
because positive-definitenes must be maintained.

No, we don't have a time for vectorizing multi-normal. Hopefully
we'll get it done by the end of the summer. It really shouldn't
be too much work to at least do the simple cases allowing an array
of outcomes, which is where the speed bump will come from.
I've added a high-priority feature request for this because we really
should have it in place and it's not that hard:

http://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/589

To answer your other question, if you want the full log likelihood of
the model, you're not including the contribution of the multi_normal_cholesky
terms in the model. If they're only being used to generate predictive
quantities, that's OK. What we also need to do is add the _rng function
for multi_normal_cholesky, and then they could be moved to the generated
quantities block. Hence, another issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/590

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] priors when using cholesky_decomposition
parts:
Sorry --- didn't read your model that closely. I see that
you have both
log_lik[i] <- multi_normal_cholesky_log(y[i],mu[i],Ly);}

and

y[i] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu[i], Ly);

This is doing redundant work. You can either

1. add

increment_log_prob(sum(log_lik));

to the model and remove the y[i] ~ ...

or

2. Calculate log_lik in the generated quantities block.

Andrew prefers (2) in order to keep the calculation of WAIC
separate from the model and for efficiency.

We're in the middle of writing up some recommendations on
WAIC calculations, which we'll share when they're done.

- Bob
